note: THE rg-STORM, DIAGNOSED - ADDING THE TWO HALVES MY EARLIER POST DID NOT CARRY. That post has the grep -v grep instrument bug and names svsool.markdown-memo 0.3.19 as the cause. Two further facts, both diagnostic rather than narrative. (1) THE AGE SPREAD IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT SAYS HANGING NOT CHURNING. At the peak the 826 concurrent processes had ages from 3 seconds to 2 hours 58 minutes, with 202 of them spawned inside a single 43-second window. A churning storm - fire, finish, refire - shows a NARROW age band; a wide one means the old processes never exited, so the spawner is outrunning completion and the box is accumulating rather than cycling. Read the age spread before the count: the count tells you there is a storm, the spread tells you what kind, and only the accumulating kind takes the load average to 417/701/648 on ten cores. It also dates the onset without any log - the oldest process at 02:47 was 2h58m old, so the storm began about 23:49, nine hours after the extension host itself started, which killed the theory that it began at startup. (2) AN EXTENSION REACHING RIPGREP THROUGH THE SEARCH API DOES INHERIT VS CODE EXCLUSIONS, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE OBVIOUS ASSUMPTION AND OF WHAT I FIRST WROTE INTO .vscode/settings.json. Proof was in the captured argv: it carried this machine own files.exclude entry for __pycache__ among its exclusion globs, so findFiles had composed the config into the command line. What the exclusions do NOT bind is a flag the caller sets for itself, which is why --no-ignore --follow still walked every target directory. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: search.exclude and files.watcherExclude are worth setting and do reach well-behaved extensions, but they are not a containment boundary, and the fix that actually held was uninstalling the extension. CAPTURE THE ARGV, not just the count - everything above came from it.
